hero.title: GEarheads meets GE Elfuns.
hero.subtitle: The GE Elfuns are GE's retiree network — engineers, project managers, and executives from GE Healthcare, Energy, and Manufacturing. GEarheads presents to the group regularly, building toward a mentorship pipeline that connects decades of industrial experience with the next generation of builders.

heroPhoto.caption: GEarheads team presenting to the GE Elfuns retiree group

impact.label: Why this partnership matters
impact.text: Most high school robotics teams never get access to the kind of engineering experience the Elfuns bring. Building this relationship works both ways: retirees learn what FIRST and FTC actually look like, and the team gets exposure to professionals who've solved real problems at industrial scale. It's about raising awareness as much as opening a door to mentorship.

approach.label: Why This Partnership
approach.heading: Two communities that were already connected.
approach.body:
GEarheads isn't named for GE by accident. GE Healthcare employees were among our earliest supporters, and they brought an engineering culture with them — rigorous process, structured design review, data-driven decisions. Our DHF, FMEA, and DOE testing all trace back to GE practice.

The Elfuns are retirees who spent careers doing that kind of engineering. When we present to them, we're not performing for a general audience — they recognize DHF notation, have run FMEA on real products, and know a Monte Carlo simulation is serious engineering. They ask hard questions and connect our challenges to problems they spent years solving in industry.

The long-term goal is a formal mentorship pipeline, with Elfuns members serving as design advisors. It's not there yet, but every presentation moves it closer.

inlinePhoto.caption: An Elfuns member in conversation with the GEarheads team

facets.label: Presentations Overview
facets.tagline: Connecting the GEarheads story to GE's legacy.
facets.description: GEarheads has presented to the GE Elfuns, walking them through what FTC is and what we build. We tailor each talk to the audience, drawing parallels between our robot's engineering challenges and the problems Elfuns spent careers solving at GE — our DHF process, Monte Carlo simulation, DOE work on the launcher.
highlights: Tailored to career engineers and technical leaders
Covers our real DHF process and design tools
Parallels robotics with industrial engineering
Frames FIRST as a real program, not a hobby
Builds credibility within the GE community

facets.label: Technical Mentorship Pipeline
facets.tagline: Decades of expertise, one introduction away.
facets.description: The biggest long-term opportunity is a technical mentorship pipeline. The Elfuns include engineers with deep experience in manufacturing, controls, and medical devices — directly useful to a team that runs CNC mills and writes control software. A formal relationship would mean a second opinion on a mechanism, or guidance on applying DOE in practice.
highlights: Career engineers in manufacturing and controls
Directly relevant: CNC, controls, materials, systems
Potential for structured design reviews
Bridges school and industrial-scale engineering
Groundwork laid through ongoing presentations

facets.label: Expanding FIRST Awareness
facets.tagline: FIRST reaches communities it has never reached before.
facets.description: Most FIRST outreach flows toward younger students and their families. This runs the other way — bringing FIRST to people who've already finished their careers. When a retired GE engineer understands what FTC is, that spreads: at a grandchild's school, or in a word put in for a rookie team's sponsorship.
highlights: Reaches retiree networks outside the usual school pipeline
Retirees can champion FIRST to grandchildren, local orgs
Multiplies reach beyond student-facing outreach
Builds a network of informed FIRST advocates
Each visit strengthens the case for future support

facets.label: The GE↔GEarheads Connection
facets.tagline: The name is not a coincidence.
facets.description: GEarheads isn't named for GE by accident. GE Healthcare employees were among our founding supporters, and their engineering culture shaped how we operate. The Elfuns partnership extends that: they know what GE Healthcare built, and our tools — DHF, FMEA, DOE — were refined over decades in that same environment.
highlights: Co-founded with support from GE Healthcare employees
Our DHF, FMEA, DOE practices come from GE methodology
Deepens the founding GE connection
Shared language makes it substantive, not ceremonial
A rare tie to a major industrial engineering legacy
